findings.title: compile() writes str to a binary-mode NamedTemporaryFile
findings.impact: tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile defaults to mode 'w+b'. Under Python 3, f.write(source) raises TypeError when source is str, so compile() fails when no source_fn is given. The module uses __future__ imports, which suggests it also targets Python 3. On Windows, the temp file can't be reopened by name while it is still open, so the subprocess f2py call would fail there too. The source_fn branch opens the file in text mode, so the two branches behave differently.
findings.recommendation: Create the file in text mode, for example NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.f', delete=False). Remove it explicitly after the build, or write into a mkdtemp directory. Make both branches use the same mode.
